concurrent_fusion.finding: Three relation surface families lowered to identical typed Relation IR semantic hashes in a bounded oracle; this supports using typed IR as the semantic comparator but does not select a preferred surface syntax.

hypotheses.statement: Most remaining G9 rule self-conformance failures are surface-form problems that can be normalized into the existing call/operator expression basis without adding new semantic primitives, with typed Relation IR as the semantic oracle.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: The prose-like rule forms encode distinctions that calls/operators cannot preserve.
hypotheses.test: Parse all 58 current G9+dialect rule declarations under current grammar, previous minimal repair, then a bounded source-normalization candidate; compare direction with the concurrent typed Relation IR oracle.
hypotheses.result: Original 34/58 pass; previous minimal repair 38/58; normalized candidate 58/58. Concurrent relation-IR run separately found multiple safe surface families mapping to identical typed IR semantic hashes.
hypotheses.falsifier: Full G9 source->parser->AST->typed-IR comparison shows any normalization changes relation identity, effect ordering, provenance or semantic hash.

hypotheses.statement: The dialect registry requires an explicit typed method-signature declaration production rather than treating every interface member as a field/action.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Existing field/call grammar is sufficient after source normalization.
hypotheses.test: Parse all 9 current interface declarations against the current block/field shape.
hypotheses.result: 6/9 pass; Projectable, Verifiable and Incremental fail exactly at typed method signatures.
hypotheses.falsifier: A deterministic normalization into existing typed constructs preserves identical canonical method semantics without a new declaration form.

hypotheses.statement: G9 optional fallback semantics must be made explicit before canonicalization because eager versus lazy fallback is observably different and may change effects.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: The current receipt? or residual form has an already-defined unambiguous semantics elsewhere in the admitted stack.
hypotheses.test: Current expression fails grammar; local lazy/eager fallback probe records whether fallback executes when receipt is present.
hypotheses.result: Current form fails. Lazy present does not evaluate fallback; eager present does. Observable behavior differs.
hypotheses.falsifier: An admitted authoritative semantic contract is found that defines the form and its evaluation order, and the compiler implements it without ambiguity.

hypotheses.statement: The flat expr grammar needs an explicit precedence/associativity contract before deterministic canonical semantic hashing.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: All admitted expressions are intentionally flat/left-associative or typing uniquely resolves them.
hypotheses.test: Evaluate 1+2*3 under flat-left-fold versus multiplication precedence and inspect current mixed comparison/boolean G9 rules.
hypotheses.result: Observable results differ (9 vs 7); G9 contains mixed >= and && expressions.
hypotheses.falsifier: Current canonicalizer/spec already defines and validates a unique precedence table for every admitted operator.

hypotheses.statement: Research-candidate .clay artifacts must not automatically be treated as BASE admitted compile units.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: The BASE grammar should immediately parse every research candidate surface.
hypotheses.test: Inspect current stack dynamic-binding candidate against G9 declaration grammar.
hypotheses.result: Candidate uses projection, experiment, hypothesis, counterhypothesis and falsifier declarations absent from G9 grammar while explicitly marked RESEARCH_CANDIDATE.
hypotheses.falsifier: A current compilation-unit registry explicitly admits these declaration forms into the BASE language contract.
